newsitem.title: GERMANY: German steel workers to protest at possible merger.
newsitem.headline: German steel workers to protest at possible merger.

text.p: Thousands of German steel workers downed tools and planned to demonstrate on Tuesday against a possible hostile takeover bid by industrial giant Krupp of Thyssen AG, works councils said.

Just days after miners' protests virtually besieged Bonn to protest against coal subsidy cuts, fears that a giant merger in Germany's Ruhr Valley industrial heartland could cost thousands of workers their jobs looked set to spark a new protest wave.

The demonstration was called a day after Thyssen AG released a combative statement saying Krupp planned a hostile take-over of the company and vowed to use "all appropriate measures" to ward off any grab for control by its rival.
"We will not just sit back and let this happen to us. Basically this is undiluted capitalism, pure Wild West methods," Willy Siegerer, the deputy head of the Thyssen works council, told German radio.

"We believe that if Thyssen is bought by Krupp then it will be broken up," Siegerer said, adding that the works council had contacted members of Thyssen's supervisory board but they could not shed any more light on Krupp's exact plans.

The works councils of both German steel firms said workers had already stopped work and would make their way to the western city of Essen to protest outside the headquarters of Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp later on Tuesday morning.

Dieter Kroll, the head of Thyssen works council, told NRW radio earlier that both he and the head of Krupp's works council Werner Nass feared such a takeover could mean the loss of 10,000 jobs in the state of North-Rhine Westphalia.
Nass told NRW radio that the merger could mean the loss of 5,500 to 6,000 jobs in the city of Dortmund alone and that this would mean an unemployment rate of about 20 percent there.
